name: Manikkavannar Temple, Tirumarugal
tradition: Shaiva — a Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung in the Tevaram
summary: Tirumarugal, near Nannilam, is the setting of one of the tenderest miracles of the Tevaram age: here the child-saint Tirugnana Sambandar is said to have sung a snakebitten bridegroom back to life and seen the young couple wedded, with Shiva himself standing witness. The lord is worshipped as Manikkavannar, the gem-hued one — also called Ratnagireeswarar — a Paadal Petra Sthalam with a self-manifested lingam, and the nearby Vinayaka, who helped undo the poison, is honoured as Vitam-teertha Vinayakar.

sections.history: Tirumarugal is an ancient Shaiva village in the Nannilam country, revered in the seventh-century Tevaram and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. The lingam is held to be self-manifested, and the sthala vriksham is the marugal tree that gives the place its name. The stone temple is of the Chola period with later additions; its fame, however, rests chiefly on the great Tevaram miracle that unfolded here, which has kept the village in devotional memory for well over a thousand years.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan, with a gopuram, prakara and the sanctum of Manikkavannar — Ratnagireeswarar — housing the self-manifested lingam. Within the complex stands the shrine of Vitam-teertha Vinayakar, the Ganesha tied to the poison-removing miracle, whose name carries 'vitam,' poison. The marugal (sthala) tree and the temple tank complete a compact, atmospheric village shrine shaped by a single tender story.
sections.legends: The legend of Tirumarugal is beloved across the Tamil country. A young couple, in love against their families' wishes, were to be wed, but the bridegroom died of a snakebite. The child-saint Sambandar, moved by the grief, sang a Tevaram hymn to Shiva, and the young man rose alive; the marriage was then solemnised, with the lord himself as witness when doubt was cast on the union. The nearby Vinayaka, said to have aided in drawing out the poison, is honoured as Vitam-teertha Vinayakar. The story makes Tirumarugal a place devotees associate with healing, marriage and the undoing of grief.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi observances and the annual Brahmotsavam. The association with Sambandar's miracle gives the days honouring the saint a special warmth, and couples and families come with prayers for marriage, for children and for relief from the fear of snakebite and poison.
sections.experience: Tirumarugal is a quiet village temple whose power is the tenderness of its story. Pilgrims come knowing the tale of the revived bridegroom and the witnessing lord, and the darshan of Manikkavannar carries the sense of a grace that answers love and grief alike. For many it is a place of hope at the thresholds of life — marriage, healing, and new beginnings.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirumarugal is in the Nannilam area (Tiruvarur/Nagapattinam district), about 6-7 km from Tiruppugalur and roughly 20 km from Tiruvarur; the nearest rail heads are Nannilam and Tiruvarur, with local buses and taxis to the village.
